description: Chaotic low-frequency oscillator running the Halvorsen attractor, a set of equations whose orbit never repeats, giving four wandering voltages

params.text: Sets how fast the system travels along its orbit, from a thousandth of full rate at the bottom of its travel to full rate at the top
Adjusts one constant in the equations, 1.23 to 1.63, which changes the shape of the orbit; below that the system runs away and above it it stops being chaotic
Sets the voltage the four outputs span, from about ±0.1V at the bottom of its travel through ±5V at the centre to about ±10V fully clockwise

outputs.text: The x coordinate of the system, scaled to the range set by the scale knob
The y coordinate of the system, scaled to the range set by the scale knob
The z coordinate of the system, scaled to the range set by the scale knob
x plus y minus z, the maker's own fourth output, scaled to the range set by the scale knob

notes: the system is only calculated while a cable is patched to one of the four outputs.
a chaotic system is not held inside the range the scale knob sets, and the outputs will now and then go above or below it; put a clamp or a limiter after them where that matters.
